definitions.explanation: Addressing the root cause of a problem rather than surface symptoms. Used to describe reforms, changes, or solutions that go to the very foundation of an issue.

examples.japanese: {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な{改革|かいかく}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
{問題|もんだい}の{抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な{解決|かいけつ}にはまだ{時間|じかん}がかかる。
examples.english: It will still take time to achieve a fundamental solution to the problem.

examples.japanese: {制度|せいど}を{抜本的|ばっぽんてき}に{見直|みなお}さなければ、{同|おな}じ{問題|もんだい}が{繰|く}り{返|かえ}されるだろう。
examples.english: Unless the system is fundamentally re-examined, the same problems will recur.

notes:
USAGE:
Literally means "pulling out the root" ({抜|ぬ}く = pull out, {本|もと} = root/origin). Used as a na-adjective, almost always with な or に. Frequently appears in formal contexts such as political speeches, news reports, and policy discussions. Implies that half-measures are insufficient and deep structural change is required.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な{改革|かいかく}: fundamental reform
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な{見直|みなお}し: fundamental review
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な{対策|たいさく}: drastic measures
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}に{変|か}える: to change fundamentally

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {根本的|こんぽんてき}: fundamental (similar but broader; less reform-oriented)
- {徹底的|てっていてき}: thorough (emphasizes completeness rather than depth)
